Use a proper toast/notification UI for user feedback. If any logging is needed for debugging, gate it on `import.meta.env.DEV` as is done in ErrorBoundary.jsx. |
| medium | Hardcoded placeholder email in Paystack deposit flow | src/components/DepositForm.jsx:29: `email: 'user@example.com'` passed to PaystackPop.setup(). Paystack requires a real customer email for receipts and fraud detection; using a placeholder means all payments are associated with a non-existent customer. | Read the current user's email from the auth context/hook (`const { user } = useAuth()`) and pass `email: user.email`. If the user is not authenticated, gate the form behind auth and never reach the Paystack call. |
| medium | WebSocket authentication — no token attached at connection time | src/hooks/useWebSocket.js:51-58 — WebSocket URLs (/ws/comms, /ws/voice, /ws/game/:id) are constructed with no Authorization header or query token. The WebSocket API does not support custom headers from the browser. The backend must therefore authenticate via the first message over the socket or via session cookie. No first-message auth frame is sent in useCommsSocket.js or useGameSession.js before any sensitive message. | Implement a handshake: immediately after onopen, send `{ type: 'auth', token: localStorage.getItem('token') }` and require the backend to validate it before accepting any other message type. Alternatively, move to cookie-based session auth (HttpOnly cookie is automatically sent with WebSocket upgrades), which resolves this and the localStorage finding simultaneously. |
| medium | Voice room join token sent unprotected over WS message | src/hooks/useCommsSocket.js:265: `sendVoiceSignal({ type: 'voice_join', room_id: roomId, token })`. The join token from api.voice.joinToken() is passed as a plain JSON field over the WebSocket, which is itself unauthenticated (see above). Any WebSocket sniffer on an http:// connection or an MitM can capture the voice join token. | Enforce WSS (wss://) in all production deployments and add the per-connection auth handshake noted above. The voice join token sent after a valid auth handshake is acceptable; without it, voice rooms are effectively unprotected. |
| medium | Server-url from play manifest used directly as WebSocket endpoint — SSRF/redirect risk | src/hooks/usePlayManifest.js:73: manifest.server_url fetched from the backend. src/pages/Playground.jsx:111-112: `const wsEndpoint = manifest?.server_url ?? null; const ws = connectWebSocket(wsEndpoint)`. If the backend is compromised or a developer game entry has a malicious server_url, the browser opens a WebSocket to an attacker-controlled endpoint, sending `{ type: 'join_game', playerId: user.id }`. | Validate server_url before use: confirm it starts with wss:// (or ws:// only in development), and ideally confirm it matches an allowlist of known game-server domains. Reject and display an error if the URL fails validation. |
| medium | frontend/nginx.fly.conf has no security headers and proxies backend over plain HTTP | frontend/nginx.fly.conf:23-31 — proxy_pass is `http://magnetite.fly.dev:8080` (plain HTTP), no security headers at all (no X-Frame-Options, no CSP, no Referrer-Policy). Even if Fly terminates TLS at the edge, the backend leg is plaintext. | Add the same security headers as nginx.conf (X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy) plus a CSP. If the Fly backend is on the same private network, the HTTP internal leg may be acceptable, but document it explicitly. Add HSTS if the public edge is always HTTPS. |
| low | AuthContext (context/AuthContext.jsx) is a dead mock that ships alongside useAuth hook | src/context/AuthContext.jsx:23-38 — login() and register() fabricate mock tokens ('mock-jwt-token-' + Date.now()) and never call the real API. Token validation in useEffect is also entirely mocked (line 15-16). This file co-exists with the real src/hooks/useAuth.js. If any component is accidentally wired to useAuth from this context instead of the hook, it silently accepts any email/password without server auth. | Delete src/context/AuthContext.jsx entirely, or replace it with a thin re-export of useAuth from the hook. Remove the mock login/register implementations to prevent accidental use. |
| low | Stale USDC/crypto copy in Login.jsx marketing panel | src/pages/Login.jsx:71 — `<span className='auth-hero-stat-value'>USDC</span>` with label 'instant payouts'. DECISIONS.md D-PAY-1/D-PAY-6 explicitly removes all crypto/USDC references; this copy was not updated. | Replace 'USDC / instant payouts' stat with 'Wise / fiat payouts' or similar fiat-accurate copy per DECISIONS.md D-PAY-6. |

## Missing Features vs Vision (DECISIONS.md §1/§1b/§4b + Economy)

_The codebase has covered a remarkable breadth in its autonomous wave program, but a cohesive set of product-critical features are genuinely absent or skeleton-only. The most launch-blocking gaps are: (1) the TOTP second factor is set up but never enforced at login so it is security theatre; (2) subscription upgrades/downgrades have no backend endpoint and the frontend calls a non-existent /api/subscriptions/upgrade route; (3) real-time notification delivery is HTTP-poll-only on the frontend (NotificationContext.jsx) despite a WS endpoint existing on the backend — users will not see live alerts; (4) the moderation pipeline for reported reviews has no admin visibility or action surface; (5) the leaderboard has no seasonality link to the seasons system in points_ledger; (6) the search is ILIKE substring-only, no relevance ranking or full-text index; (7) the friend system has no endpoint to list pending/sent requests and no way to cancel a sent request; (8) the Wise payout KYC only collects email or US-ACH — IBAN, the most common non-US path, has no type field in WiseClient; (9) the web WASM game client path exists only as a documented Bucket-D item; and (10) no content-rating, tax-withholding, or i18n layer exists anywhere in the stack. Several more medium-severity gaps follow._

| Sev | Finding | Evidence | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| critical | TOTP 2FA exists but is never checked at login — security theatre | backend/src/api/auth.rs:164-190: the login handler selects only (id, username, email, password_hash) and never reads totp_enabled or totp_secret. backend/src/api/auth.rs:572-690 implements setup/verify/disable but these are never called from the login path. | Add a totp_challenge step to login: if the user row has totp_enabled=true, issue a short-lived challenge token instead of a full session, require the client to POST /auth/2fa/challenge with the code, then create the session. Without this, enabling 2FA has zero security effect. |
| critical | Subscription upgrade/downgrade/proration entirely missing from backend | backend/src/api/subscriptions.rs:177-411: only subscribe (new) and cancel_subscription exist. The frontend client calls /api/subscriptions/upgrade (src/api/client.js:78) which is not mounted anywhere in main.rs. No proration or mid-cycle tier change logic exists anywhere in the services. | Add PUT /api/v1/subscriptions/upgrade that cancels the current active subscription, issues a prorated Paystack charge for the delta, and creates a new subscription at the target tier for the remaining period. Register it in main.rs. Wire the frontend to that real endpoint. |
| high | Real-time notification delivery not connected — frontend polls REST only | src/context/NotificationContext.jsx:14-36: only calls api.notifications.list() on mount; no WebSocket is opened. src/hooks/useNotifications.js:4 has a comment 'Real-time notification updates arrive via the comms WebSocket' but the CommsProvider does not push into NotificationContext. The backend WS endpoint ws/notifications exists (backend/src/api/notifications.rs:342) and broadcasts correctly, but no frontend code connects to it. | In NotificationProvider (or CommsContext), open a WebSocket to /ws/notifications after login, parse incoming NotificationBroadcast JSON frames, and call addNotification. This is the only way users receive friend-request, payout, and achievement alerts without a page refresh. |
| high | Reported reviews: no admin moderation surface — reports go into the DB and are never acted upon | backend/src/api/reviews.rs:362-430: report_review stores rows in review_reports table. backend/src/api/admin.rs:1185-1300: the admin router has no route for listing or dismissing review reports. admin.rs lines 1-1302 searched for 'review_report' — zero hits. | Add GET /api/v1/admin/review-reports (paginated, filter by reason/status) and POST /api/v1/admin/review-reports/:id/dismiss (or /action with remove_review option). Wire it to the Admin Moderation page. Without this, the report flow is user-facing theater. |
| high | Leaderboard seasonality not connected to the seasons/points system | backend/src/services/leaderboard.rs: uses Redis sorted sets with keys leaderboard:{game_id}; the archive_and_reset method exists (has an archive_key) but is never called from a scheduled job or the points season-reset endpoint. backend/src/api/points.rs:60 defines season_id on point balance but leaderboard scores have no season dimension. Services/achievements.rs has no seasonal reset either. | Call LeaderboardService::archive_and_reset from the points season-reset handler (backend/src/api/points.rs line ~249). Add a season_label parameter to the Redis sorted set key so per-season historical boards are addressable. Expose GET /api/v1/leaderboard?season_id= on the read path. |
| high | Friend system: no endpoint to list pending/incoming requests, no cancel-sent-request | backend/src/api/social.rs:550-595 (router): routes are GET / (friends), POST /request, POST /accept/:id, POST /reject/:id, DELETE /:id (remove), POST /block/:id. No GET /pending (incoming), no GET /sent (outgoing), no DELETE /request/:id (cancel sent). FriendService.get_pending_requests exists in backend/src/services/friends.rs:209 but is never wired to a route. | Add GET /friends/pending (calls FriendService::get_pending_requests for the current user) and DELETE /friends/request/:id for cancellation. Wire pending count to the notification bell. This is a day-1 UX expectation for any social feature. |
| high | Email verification not enforced at login — unverified accounts can do everything | backend/src/api/auth.rs:164-190: the login handler never reads the email_verified column. The query at line 169-170 selects only (id, username, email, password_hash). Unverified users can deposit funds, publish games, and withdraw. backend/src/services/wallet.rs:280 mentions a KYC limit but email_verified is not the gate. | Read email_verified in the login query. Either block login for unverified users (return 403 with a resend link), or issue a restricted token that is rejected by a middleware guard on financial and developer endpoints. At minimum, block deposit/withdraw/publish until email is verified. |
| high | Wise payout KYC only supports US-ACH and email — IBAN (international) missing | backend/src/services/wise.rs:150-169: only two type_str branches exist: 'email' and 'aba' (US ABA routing). The RecipientDetails struct (lines 84-105) has no iban or swift fields. Wise supports IBAN transfers as type 'iban' with sort_code/account_number for GBP or bic/iban for SEPA. The Earnings.jsx form collects freeform 'IBAN/Email/Bank account' text but the backend ignores it. | Add an IbanDetails variant to RecipientDetails (iban: String, bic: Option<String>) and a third 'iban' branch in WiseClient::create_recipient. The Earnings.jsx recipient form should split into ACH / IBAN / Email tabs so the correct fields are collected and transmitted. |
| high | Search is ILIKE substring-only — no full-text ranking, no tag/genre filter | backend/src/api/search.rs:52-90: search uses WHERE title ILIKE $1 OR description ILIKE $1 with a CASE-based title-first tie-break. No GIN index, no to_tsvector/ts_rank, no category/tag filter, no minimum-score threshold. With even a few hundred games the ILIKE scan will be slow and results will have no quality signal. | Add a tsvector generated column to games (GIN index) and use ts_rank in ORDER BY. Expose category_id, min_rating, and is_free filters as query params. This matters for marketplace discovery once more than a handful of games exist. |
| medium | Game version rollback UX missing — promote-only, no demote/rollback | backend/src/api/distribution.rs:98-106: only promote_version exists (sets is_live=true on one version). backend/src/services/distribution.rs:120,154-164 atomically demotes old live and promotes new but there is no endpoint to revert to a previous live version by specifying a prior version_id. The developer dashboard has no rollback button. | Expose PUT /api/v1/distribution/:game_id/versions/:version_id/rollback (or reuse promote_version with any historical version_id). Add a 'Set Live' / 'Rollback' button next to each version row in the developer build-status view. |
| medium | Developer analytics: no funnel/cohort/conversion metrics, no revenue time-series per game | backend/src/api/developer.rs:465-543: get_game_analytics returns daily active players (30d), avg session duration, total revenue, session count. There is no revenue over time chart, no purchase funnel, no churn rate, no geographic breakdown. The platform admin has analytics_revenue (daily/weekly/monthly time-series) but developers do not. | Add a daily_revenue_chart field to GameAnalytics: query game_revenue GROUP BY DATE in the same 30-day window. Add a purchases_count from store_purchases WHERE game_id. This is what developers need to decide pricing and monetization strategy. |
| medium | Subscription lifecycle: cancel sets status=cancelled immediately, not cancel-at-period-end | backend/src/api/subscriptions.rs:342-411: cancel_subscription executes UPDATE user_subscriptions SET status = 'cancelled' immediately. The PaymentService struct has a cancel_at_period_end field (backend/src/services/payment.rs:43) but the subscriptions.rs cancel path never sets it; cancellation takes effect right away rather than at the end of the paid period. | Change cancel_subscription to set status='cancel_pending', cancel_at_period_end=true, leave the subscription active until current_period_end. The renewal job should then check for cancel_at_period_end=true rows and set them to 'cancelled' at expiry. This is the standard SaaS behaviour users expect. |
| medium | Refunds/chargebacks: no mechanism exists anywhere in the stack | grep across all backend/src/ for 'refund', 'chargeback', 'dispute' returns zero results. Terms.jsx:71 says 'All game purchases are final and non-refundable unless otherwise stated by the developer'. Paystack and Wise both have refund APIs, but neither is wired. There is no admin panel action to issue a refund on a transaction. | Add POST /api/v1/admin/transactions/:id/refund that calls Paystack's refund endpoint for deposits/subscriptions and Wise's cancellation endpoint for payouts, then records a reversal transaction. | medium | Web WASM game client path: browser cannot play Bevy games — documented as Bucket D | The core vision (DECISIONS.md §1: 'Clients compile Bevy → WASM (browser)') requires the browser play-flow to load a .wasm file and run it. game-client-bevy/ exists but build.sh / wasm32 CI path for fps/motorsport is explicitly Bucket D (GAPS.md lines 154-155). The Playground.jsx connects a game WebSocket but renders only a canvas element — no .wasm loader, no wasm-bindgen JS glue, no CDN URL for the artifact. | This is the single largest gap between vision and reality for end-users. The minimum launchable path: CI builds the WASM artifact, uploads to S3/CDN (artifact_url in game_artifacts), and the Playground page fetches the play manifest (already wired) then dynamically loads the JS glue bootstrapped by wasm-bindgen. The GitHub CI wasm-pack runner is the external blocker, but the Playground loader code can and should be written now. |
| medium | Content rating / age restriction system entirely absent | grep across the entire codebase for 'content_rating', 'age_rating', 'PEGI', 'ESRB', 'mature_content' returns zero results. The games table and game registration flow have no age-rating field. Marketplaces distributing games to minors without content ratings face regulatory risk in the EU (PEGI) and US. | Add a content_rating column to games (enum: E, E10+, T, M, AO or PEGI equivalents), require developers to select one during game submission, display it on the GameDetail and Marketplace cards, and provide an optional age-gate on the play page for M/AO titles. |
| medium | Tax/withholding and KYC-for-payouts: Wise-level identity verification not collected | backend/src/services/wise.rs: Wise requires identity documents for transfers above certain thresholds and US-resident developers receiving significant income need a W-9/W-8. The services/verification.rs:16-21 has a KYCVerified enum variant but backend/src/api/*.rs has no handler that transitions a user to KYCVerified status — it is read at wallet.rs:280 for a threshold check but never set. Terms.jsx:124 says 'Developers are responsible for their own tax obligations' but the platform collects no tax documentation. | Add a developer onboarding flow: before first payout create, require name, country, and a tax form choice (W-9 for US, self-certification for non-US). Store as kyc_status='pending' until verified. Block PayoutService::process_pending_payouts for payouts where the recipient's KYC status is not 'verified' or 'exempt'. | medium | Anti-abuse rate limits do not cover chat messages or review submissions | backend/src/middleware/rate_limit.rs:209-219: get_rate_limit_config only specifies distinct limits for /api/auth/, /api/wallet/, and /api/games — all other paths get the default 200 req/min. backend/src/ws/comms.rs and backend/src/api/messages.rs have no per-user message-rate check. backend/src/api/reviews.rs:146-200: create_review has no rate limit beyond the global 200/min. | In the comms WS handler, track message timestamps per connection and drop/disconnect clients exceeding e.g. 10 messages/second. Add a specific rate config entry for /api/channels/*/messages and /api/games/*/reviews (e.g. 5 req/min for reviews) in get_rate_limit_config. |
| medium | Friend list missing blocked-user view and unblock endpoint is not routed | backend/src/api/social.rs:550-595: POST /block/:id exists but there is no GET /blocked (list all blocked users) and no DELETE /block/:id (unblock) in the router. This is a basic social safety feature — users need a UI to see and reverse their block list. |
| low | i18n / localization: zero infrastructure, hard-coded English only | grep across src/ for 'i18n', 'locale', 'useTranslation', 'formatMessage' returns zero hits. All UI text is hard-coded English strings. The platform targets international developers (Wise IBAN, Paystack for Africa/LatAm), but price display, date formats, and UI text are all en-US with no abstraction layer. | For a v1 launch this is low priority but the foundation matters: adopt react-i18next, extract all user-visible strings to an en.json namespace, and add a locale selector in Settings. | low | Notification real-time: the WS endpoint at /ws/notifications requires auth middleware but is mounted outside /api/v1 without the auth layer | backend/src/main.rs:142-155: the app mounts notification_ws_handler.router() directly on the top-level Router, outside the api_v1 block which carries the versioning + rate-limit layers. backend/src/api/notifications.rs:362: handle_notification_connection uses Extension(user_id) but the auth middleware (from_fn_with_state auth_middleware) is not applied to this route in main.rs. | Apply the auth middleware to the /ws/notifications route in main.rs (use .layer(from_fn_with_state(pool.clone(), middleware::auth_middleware)) on the handler, or move it inside api_v1 under a /ws sub-router). Without this, the WS endpoint is publicly accessible. |
| low | Developer analytics: no geographic or device breakdown, no store conversion funnel | backend/src/api/developer.rs:465-543: GameAnalytics has daily_active_players, session_duration_stats, revenue_breakdown only. No geographic data (country from IP), no device type (mobile vs desktop), no store_purchases funnel (views → add-to-wishlist → purchase). | Capture country from the IP header on session creation (MaxMind GeoLite2 or ipinfo.io). Add a daily_store_conversions query joining store_items and store_purchases. These signals are essential for pricing and localization decisions. |

Restart behaviour is honest: `discovery_ads` persists rows so a restart doesn't blank the phonebook, but nothing there is authoritative — every lease lapses within 10 min unless the node heartbeats, so even a restored-from-backup tracker converges to whoever is actually up. - [Wave2-DI] done — `magnetite-seams/src/{discovery.rs,lib.rs}`, `backend/src/api/discovery.rs`, `backend/src/services/provisioning.rs`, `backend/migrations/20260719_discovery_node_labels.sql`, `backend/tests/discovery_http_tests.rs`, `magnetite-runtime/src/{node.rs,tracker.rs,lib.rs}`, `magnetite-cli/src/main.rs`, `magnetite-e2e/tests/decentralized_loop.rs`, `src/hooks/useDiscovery.js`, `src/pages/{ServerBrowser.jsx,ServerBrowser.css}`, `src/pages/__tests__/ServerBrowser.test.jsx`, `docs|site/screenshots/**` — **The server browser is wired to reality.** (1) SHAPE RECONCILED, both sides, with provenance made explicit rather than blurred. The frontend mocked `game_title`/`node_operator`/`region`/`version` and `b3:`-prefixed hashes; none of those existed on the wire, so live data rendered `undefined`. Resolution, field by field: **game title/version are TRACKER-RESOLVED** — the backend now joins `game_artifacts`→`games`/`game_versions` on the announced content hash (`DISTINCT ON`, newest successful artifact) and returns `game_title`/`game_version`, which are **null for any hash this tracker has never indexed** (the normal case in a decentralized network, not an error); the lookup **fails soft** (a catalog query error logs and serves hashes, never fails the phonebook) because the authoritative half of the response is the signed ads. **Operator/region are NODE-DECLARED** — a tracker cannot verify where a box is or who runs it, so they became `Option<String>` fields *inside* the signed `SessionAd` body (covered by `signing_bytes`, so a relay cannot relabel someone else's box) and are rendered with a `self-declared` chip and a "signed by its key, but not verified by any tracker" tooltip. A phonebook reports what nodes claim; it does not certify it. **Hash form is plain hex everywhere** — `b3:` is gone from the frontend's data expectations; the `BLAKE3` chip is a rendering choice. The mocks are now a faithful mirror of the real payload *including its nulls*, with two rows deliberately exercising the degraded paths (uncatalogued hash; node that declared no operator/region and publishes no occupancy counters). Every nullable field degrades: unknown title falls back to the short content address (rendered ONCE, as the title, not duplicated as title+chip), missing version → "not in this tracker's catalog", no labels → "no operator declared", absent `players`/`max_players` → "not reported" while the *signed* `free_slots` is still shown. Also made the network summary honest: "independent operators" counted self-declared names, so it now counts **distinct `node_key`s** — the one thing on that row that is actually proven. (2) TRACKER HEARTBEAT (the functional gap): `run_node` had no renew task, so a long-lived node silently dropped out of the phonebook when its lease expired. Added `node::{Heartbeat, spawn_heartbeat, DEFAULT_LEASE_SECS}` — renews every `lease/2` with ±10% jitter (many nodes booted by one orchestrator would otherwise hit a tracker in lockstep), retries failures with exponential backoff from 1s **capped at the renew interval** (never back off past it — the lease is ticking), and `run_node` now stops the heartbeat and **retracts the ad on exit, clean or not**. Required a `Discovery::withdraw` default method (no-op default; `LanDiscovery` removes the slot, `TrackerDiscovery` delegates to a new `TrackerClient::withdraw` that the HTTP client wires to its existing *signed* `SignedWithdraw` call — previously that method existed but nothing reached it). Added `FanoutDiscovery` (announce succeeds if ANY backend accepted — one dead tracker must never stop a node hosting; `find` merges and de-dups on `(game,node)`) so the CLI's LAN ad **and** its `TRACKER_URL` ad are announced, renewed and retracted through one handle; previously the CLI announced to the tracker once, out-of-band, and never renewed it. **Two real bugs found and fixed while testing this:** a lost-wakeup race (`notify_waiters` drops the stop signal if the task is not yet parked, so shutdown blocked for a whole interval — the node-tests suite took 319s; `notify_one` is permit-based and fixed it, suite now 1.06s), and a 2s minimum-lease clamp that silently overrode short leases. (3) LIVE HTTP TEST (the flagged gap): `backend/tests/discovery_http_tests.rs` binds a **real TCP socket on an ephemeral port**, serves the real axum router, and speaks HTTP with reqwest — 8 tests. The pool is `connect_lazy`, so **no Postgres and nothing external is required**. Being honest about the split: every *rejection* path is fully proven over the wire (unsigned, price-tampered, key-relabelled, operator-relabelled, lapsed lease, over-long lease, garbage bodies, non-hex game filter, forged withdrawal) because verification runs entirely before any query — that is the security-relevant half and the half a fail-open would live in, and the tests assert those return 4xx *without* reaching the DB. The *success* path is proven only as far as reachability (routes mounted at the paths the node client posts to; the flattened wire form and the browser's own filter query both parse; an honest announce survives every check and reaches the storage layer). A stored-and-served round trip genuinely needs Postgres; faking it with an in-memory store would test a fake rather than the router, so that is left to an integration environment. (4) Screenshots re-run: 24 captured, 0 failed. TESTS: seams 35 (was 29), runtime 58 lib + 4 doc (was 54), backend 603 (was 587; +8 live-HTTP, +4 shape/degradation units), cli 17, sdk 316, sandbox 32, anticheat 48, e2e decentralized_loop 4, frontend vitest 535 (was 526; +9 ServerBrowser contract tests asserting no `undefined`/`NaN`/`null` renders for any row shape). 0 failures anywhere; eslint clean; 0 new clippy warnings (runtime's 5 are pre-existing in server/tick/shard). REMAINING: stored-and-served round trip needs a DB-backed integration env; `MAGNETITE_NODE_SEED` is still a stopgap for a persisted node keypair; `NodeConfig.operator`/`region` are plumbed but the CLI has no flags to set them yet; no multi-tracker gossip (fanout is static config, not discovery-of-trackers).

- [Wave3-I1] DONE — `magnetite-seams/Cargo.toml` (new `dmtap` feature, default off, **zero** new deps), `magnetite-seams/src/keyname/mod.rs` (new), `magnetite-seams/src/keyname/wordlist.rs` (new), `magnetite-seams/src/lib.rs` (feature-gated module + re-export + doc note), `magnetite-seams/tests/seam_pluggability.rs` (new), `docs/dmtap.md` (new), `docs/index.md`, `site/docs.html`, `site/docs/dmtap.md` (mirror) — **The gap this closes:** Comms (5 impls), Discovery (3) and BlobStore (2) already proved their seams pluggable, but Naming and Identity each had exactly one implementation, so nothing showed they weren't accidentally hardwired to their default. Added `KeyNameNaming`, a second real `Naming` provider behind `--features dmtap` (OFF by default): word-based, zero-authority key-names over an embedded 2048-word list (11 bits/word), plus optional `<words>@domain` display from a *local, non-authoritative* domain hint. **Honest arithmetic, stated plainly rather than papered over:** 8 words carry 88 bits and an Ed25519 key is 256, so no 8-word scheme — not ours, not DMTAP's — can losslessly encode a key. So two forms ship: `short_name` = 8 words = 88-bit domain-separated BLAKE3 fingerprint (the display name; resolves only for keys the node has *learned* out of band), and `full_name` = 24 words = 256 key bits + 8 checksum bits = 264 = 24x11 exactly (a pure encoding, exact round-trip for every key, BIP-39-*shaped* but not BIP-39). Wordlist derived mechanically from `/usr/share/dict/words` (Webster's Second "web2", **public domain**; no BIP-39 list vendored, so no Bitcoin-project licence question): keep `^[a-z]{4,7}$`, keep only the first word per 4-char prefix (every word unambiguous from its opening), sort/dedupe to 15491, take 2048 evenly spaced so names span the alphabet — and the list's invariants (2048, sorted, unique, unique 4-prefixes, ASCII) are asserted by tests so a corrupted list fails CI instead of silently renaming every key. Fail-closed throughout: unknown word, wrong word count, bad checksum, second `@`, or a domain that disagrees with the learned hint all return `None`/`Err`; a fuzz-ish junk battery (empty, control chars, astral chars, 200-word input) asserts no panic. **NOT NAMED `DmtapNaming`, deliberately:** `dmtap-core` is not on this machine and is not published, so its wordlist/packing/checksum/separator could not be read and compatibility could not be verified — names here will almost certainly NOT match DMTAP's for the same key, and putting an unverifiable compatibility claim in a *type name* is the worst place to put one. `docs/dmtap.md` says this in as many words and enumerates what awaits the real crate (`DmtapAuth`, wire-compatible names, `DmtapPubBlobStore`/MOTE, a DMTAP comms provider, and any DMTAP dependency at all — the `dmtap` feature adds none). Pluggability proof (`tests/seam_pluggability.rs`, 4 tests): one unmodified consumer written only against `dyn Naming` is driven by both `HashNaming` and `KeyNameNaming` with identical assertions, a `Box<dyn Naming>` provider-set swaps implementations with no consumer edit, and both keep raw hex resolvable so the substrate stays reachable. For Identity/Auth a *test-double* `CounterAuth` (lives only in the test file, clearly labelled) proves the seam and the generic `BuiltinProvider<A: AuthProvider>` accept a foreign impl — no second *shipped* auth provider was invented, because none is honest without an external service or the missing crate. TESTS: seams **35 (feature off, unchanged)** / **52 (feature on: 48 lib + 4 integration)**; runtime 58 + 4 doc, backend 603, cli 17, sdk 316, sandbox 32, anticheat 48, frontend vitest 535 — all unchanged, 0 failures; clippy clean with the feature on (`large_const_arrays` fixed by making the wordlist a `static`). Default build is byte-identical: no new dependencies, no new default module. REMAINING: the actual `dmtap-core` integration is blocked on the crate existing/being reachable; short-name resolution needs a real key-learning path wired from signed discovery ads (today `learn()` is called by whoever holds the key).

- [Fleet] DONE — `magnetite-runtime/src/fleet.rs` (new, ~1050 lines incl. 21 tests), `magnetite-runtime/src/shard.rs`, `magnetite-runtime/src/lib.rs`, `docs/hosting-a-server.md`, `site/docs/hosting-a-server.md` (mirror), `DECENTRALIZATION.md` §4 — **`NetworkHandoffTransport` is no longer a stub: a world can now genuinely span more than one box.** The seam, the loopback path, single-box multi-shard hosting and capacity-emergent shard counts were all already real; the wire was not, so `HandoffTransport::transfer` on the network backend returned `HandoffError::Unimplemented` and a cluster could not share a world. Built that wire. **(1) TRANSPORT CHOICE — deliberately self-contained.** Plain blocking `std::net` TCP with 4-byte-length-prefixed JSON frames (64 MiB cap, announced-oversize refused rather than allocated) and an Ed25519 handshake over the node keypair from `magnetite_seams::identity`. **No DMTAP, no libp2p, no external service, no new dependency** — cross-node handoff is core game functionality and the architecture rests on DMTAP never being load-bearing, so putting the fleet on top of an optional protocol would invert that. Blocking sockets (not tokio) because `HandoffTransport::transfer` is a *sync* trait method; threads keep the seam signature untouched. A NAT-traversing alternative behind the same seam is mentioned in docs as possible-future and is **not** implemented. **(2) PEER AUTH — the address is not the identity.** Mutual challenge/response: client sends `Hello{pubkey, nonce}`, server answers `ServerHello{pubkey, nonce, sig}` signed over `tag||PROTO||both nonces||both pubkeys`, client verifies that signature **and that the presented key equals the key it pinned in the route**, then proves its own key the same way; server additionally checks the client key against an optional allowlist *before* spending a signature on it. Both nonces enter the transcript, and every later frame is signed over `transcript = BLAKE3(client_nonce||server_nonce)`, so a captured frame cannot be lifted into another session. Connecting to the right host:port is explicitly not accepted as proof of the right node — `PeerRoute` carries `{addr, pubkey}` and the pubkey is the load-bearing half. **(3) TWO-PHASE, EPOCH-FENCED HANDOFF — the correctness core.** Authority is the pair `(shard, epoch)`. `Offer{shard, epoch=e+1, state, hash}` → target verifies signature, re-hashes the bytes against the declared BLAKE3, checks `epoch > per-shard high-water`, and **stages** it (staged is explicitly *not* authoritative, TTL 60s) → signed `Ack` → source sends `Commit` → target promotes staged→owned and answers signed `CommitAck` → **only then** does the source release authority. **Every partial failure resolves to 'source still owns it'**: connect/handshake failure, target rejection, ack timeout, mid-transfer connection drop, and target crash all return `Err` with the source's `owned` entry and its state bytes untouched (the target's stage simply expires without ever becoming authoritative). The source never discards state before a verified `CommitAck`, so **'nobody owns the shard' is unreachable**. The one genuinely ambiguous window in any 2PC — commit delivered, commit-ack lost — is resolved by the **epoch fence** rather than hidden: the target holds `e+1`, the source holds the strictly lower `e`, and since every peer refuses any offer/commit at an epoch it has already passed, the stale owner cannot hand the shard on or resurrect itself; the higher epoch deterministically wins. The same monotonic check is what kills duplicates and replayed/stale handoffs, and the reserved epoch is burnt on failure so a retry cannot collide with an offer the peer may still have staged. **(4) DETERMINISM ACROSS MIGRATION** is asserted, not assumed: a control run ticks a deterministic toy world 1..=20 on one executor; the migrated run ticks 1..=10 on node A, ships the shard over a real socket, restores on node B and ticks 11..=20 — final snapshot hashes must be **byte-identical**, and the state hash is separately asserted continuous at the boundary (source snapshot == bytes received == post-restore snapshot). A second test proves a *failed* migration is invisible to the simulation. **(5) MULTI-NODE PLACEMENT:** `SpreadScheduler` places 8 shards across two real listeners keyed by their node pubkeys with capacity 6 vs 2 — the bigger box takes 6, the smaller 2 — and node A then ships B's share over the wire; both authority tables are then asserted disjoint (no shard owned twice, none owned by nobody). A round-trip test (A→B→A) proves epochs are strictly monotonic fleet-wide and that the stale owner is refused with `NotOwner`. **(6) FAIL-CLOSED NOT WEAKENED, AND ONE PATH TIGHTENED:** `HandoffError` gained `Auth`/`NotOwner`/`Timeout`/`Transport` and lost `Unimplemented`; the doc comment now states that *every* variant means the source retains authority. `ShardedRuntime::step_with_transport` previously logged a warning and carried on when the transport failed — leaving the player routed to a shard nobody had accepted — so it now **rolls the routing table back to the source shard** and drops the event from the reported handoffs (new test with an always-failing transport). `LoopbackTransport` and the whole single-box path are untouched and still green. TESTS: runtime **80 lib + 4 doc (was 62 + 4; +21 fleet, +1 shard revert, 1 stub test rewritten)**, all over **real sockets on ephemeral ports with 2+ nodes in-process** — negatives included by design: unauthorized key rejected, wrong node key at the right address rejected, forged client signature (claims another's pubkey) rejected, ack-timeout retains authority *and* state, target crash mid-handoff retains the shard, duplicate/stale/replayed offer rejected by the fence, cross-session signature replay rejected, tampered state rejected on hash mismatch before staging, no-route and not-owner both fail closed. No regressions: cli 17, sdk 327 (234+93), sandbox 32 (29+3), anticheat 48 (40+8), e2e all green. Clippy: 0 new warnings (fixed 3 of mine; the 2 remaining in `server.rs`/`tick.rs` are pre-existing). **REMAINING / HONEST LIMITS — stated in the docs rather than implied away:** everything is proven in-process and on a LAN over real TCP; **it has NOT been run across the public internet**. There is **no NAT traversal, no hole punching and no relay**, so nodes must be directly reachable (same LAN, VPN, or public IP with the port open); WAN latency, loss, asymmetric partitions and clock skew are untested. The docs' status box and DECENTRALIZATION.md §4 now say exactly this instead of implying fleets work over the internet today. Also still open: routes are static config (`PeerRoute` is hand-registered — no discovery-driven shard→node routing table yet, though signed `SessionAd`s already carry what it would need); the WS *client connection* is not yet forwarded to the target node after a shard moves (state migrates, the player's socket does not follow); no automatic rebalancing or failure-driven re-placement; and the transport opens a fresh connection per migration rather than pooling.

- [Fleet-Routing] DONE — `magnetite-runtime/src/cluster.rs` (new, ~1080 lines incl. 20 tests), `magnetite-runtime/src/fleet.rs` (membership gate + redirect emission + 7 wire tests), `magnetite-runtime/src/lib.rs`, `docs/hosting-a-server.md`, `site/docs/hosting-a-server.md` (mirror), `DECENTRALIZATION.md` §4 — **Closes the two gaps the `Fleet` wave left open: a cluster can now configure itself, and a player's session follows a shard that moves.** `fleet` had already built the authenticated wire and the epoch-fenced two-phase handoff; nothing below weakens any of it — the handshake, key pinning, 2PC, the epoch fence, receipt gating and `KeyProvenance::for_authorization` are untouched, and every new check is additive and fail-closed. **(1) DISCOVERY-DRIVEN ROUTING — AND THE TRAP IT WOULD HAVE WALKED INTO.** `PeerRoute`s were static config (`add_route`). `RouteDirectory::observe` now derives them from the signed `SessionAd`s already flowing through the phonebook. The obvious-but-fatal version of this feature is "hand shards to whoever announced" — discovery is an **open phonebook**, anyone may announce, so that is a one-step state-exfiltration and world-takeover path: an attacker announces, receives your shards, and is now the authoritative owner. So the rule enforced here is **discovery may supply an address; only the operator may confer membership, and membership is keyed on the node's public key**. `ClusterMembership` is that operator-authorized key set and is **deny-by-default** — an empty membership authorizes *nobody*, so a missing or half-applied config hands shards to no one rather than to anyone. It is enforced at three independent points, each failing closed: `observe` checks (a) `SignedAd::verify` — forged, tampered, future-dated, over-TTL and already-expired ads die here, *before* the membership test and without teaching the directory anything — then (b) membership, then (c) a usable address; `route_for`/`live_routes` **re-check membership and the lease on every lookup**, so revocation takes effect immediately rather than waiting for a lease to lapse; and `NetworkHandoffTransport::with_membership` re-checks at **migration time, before a byte of state leaves the box**, which is what makes a *hand-registered* route to a non-member refuse too. The pinned key of a derived route comes from the **signed ad, never from the address**, so the existing handshake still aborts if the far side presents a different key — key pinning and membership are separate defences and both must pass. `ClusterMembership::allowlist()` feeds the same operator decision to `FleetNode::bind`, gating the inbound door with the identical set. **(2) SESSION FOLLOW — REDIRECT, NOT PROXY.** When a shard moved, the state migrated and the socket did not: the player was left talking to a node that no longer owned their shard. Designed as a **client redirect** deliberately — proxying through the source would make it a permanent middleman and defeat the entire point of migrating. On a **committed** migration the source mints one `SignedRedirect` per affected player carrying the target's `{addr, pubkey}`, the shard, the new epoch, an expiry and a single-use `FollowToken`, signed by the source's node key *which the client has already authenticated*. The client calls `verify_for(expected_issuer, player, now)`: the issuer check comes **first**, so a redirect signed by anyone other than the node this session is actually talking to is discarded outright — that is what makes a forged redirect inert. It then reconnects and **pins** `target_key` (same "the address is not the identity" rule). The target's `FollowAdmission::admit` fails closed on eight separate conditions, in order: token not minted for this node (`WrongTarget`), issuer not a cluster member (`IssuerNotAMember` — an outsider cannot write its own admission tickets), bad signature, expired/future-dated, wrong player, wrong shard, **epoch ≠ the epoch this node actually owns right now** (`StaleEpoch` — the handoff epoch fence extended to cover session-follow, so a redirect from a superseded migration is refused by the new owner), and nonce already redeemed (`Replayed` — one-shot). The redirect envelope's signature covers the **token's signature**, so envelope and credential cannot be mixed and matched. Crucially, `emit_redirects` is called from exactly one place — the success arm of `migrate_shard`, past the verified `CommitAck` — so a failed, timed-out or rolled-back migration (incl. the `step_with_transport` rollback path) mints nothing and no player is ever pointed at a node that did not take the shard. **TESTS: runtime 109 lib + 4 doc (was 84 + 4; +25).** Negatives are the point, so each is asserted rather than assumed. Task A: a validly-signed announcing non-member is refused (`NotAMember`) *and*, in the wire test, a **real willing listener** volunteering for a shard still gets nothing even when its route is hand-registered — state stays put; the same ad confers routing in the cluster that admitted the node and nothing in one that did not; hijacked-address and impersonated-key ads fail verification; expired-on-arrival and lapsed-lease ads are not routed to; empty membership authorizes nobody; revocation is immediate; and an ad signed by a member whose *address* is answered by a different key aborts on the pinned-key mismatch. Task B: full happy path end-to-end over real sockets (migrate → redirect → client verify → target admit) plus forged redirect (`WrongIssuer`) and tampered redirect (`BadSignature`), expired redirect refused by **both** client and target, stale-epoch redirect refused after a real A→B→A bounce, player-X token refusing player Y (at both the client and the target), shard-S token refusing shard T, single-use replay, token for node B refused at legitimate member node C, non-member issuer refused, tampered token, envelope-with-foreign-token, JSON wire round-trip, and **a failed migration emitting zero redirects**. No regressions: seams 35 / 52 (`--features keyname`), cli 17, sandbox 32, anticheat 48, e2e 18 — all green; backend 603, sdk 327 and frontend 535 untouched by construction (no backend/sdk/frontend file changed, and `backend` does not depend on `magnetite-runtime`). Clippy: **0 new warnings** (the 2 remaining in `server.rs`/`tick.rs` are pre-existing). **No new dependency, no libp2p, no external service — everything runs offline.** **REMAINING / HONEST LIMITS:** NAT traversal is still **out of scope and not implemented** — no hole punching, no relay; nodes and clients must be directly reachable, and the docs say so rather than implying otherwise. TODO: the derived route reuses the ad's `SessionAd::node` address as the handoff endpoint, so deployments that split the game port from the handoff port need an explicit handoff-address field on the ad (adding one changes `signing_bytes`, so it was left for a deliberate seam-version bump). TODO: `shard_players` is populated by the caller (`set_shard_players`/`track_player`) and by `HandoffTransport::transfer` for the crossing player — it is not yet wired into `backend/src/ws/game.rs`, so the WS layer must call it and ship `take_redirects()` down each player's socket; the crypto and the refusals are done and tested, the socket plumbing is not. TODO: `FollowAdmission` holds redeemed nonces until `clear_redeemed()` — bounded in practice by the 30s TTL but not swept automatically. Still open from the previous wave: no automatic rebalancing or failure-driven re-placement, and one TCP connection per migration rather than pooling.

- [Fleet-Follow] DONE — `magnetite-runtime/src/follow.rs` (new, `FleetSession` + 6 tests), `magnetite-runtime/src/server.rs` (listener wiring + redirect pump), `magnetite-runtime/src/connection.rs` (`register_as`), `magnetite-runtime/src/shard.rs` (`place`), `magnetite-runtime/src/fleet.rs` (`untrack_player`/`tracked_players`), `backend/magnetite-sdk/src/protocol.rs` (4 new frames), `magnetite-runtime/tests/session_follow.rs` (new, 7 socket-level tests), `magnetite-runtime/tests/redirect_fixture.rs` + `examples/redirect_fixture.rs` (new, cross-language fixture), `magnetite-web-client/src/follow.js` (new) + `follow.test.js` (21 tests) + `connection.js`, `game-client-bevy/src/app.rs`, `magnetite-e2e/*`, `magnetite-cli/src/main.rs`, `docs/hosting-a-server.md` + `site/docs/` mirror — **The redirect mechanism is now actually connected to a player's socket: the previous wave's TODO ("`shard_players` is caller-populated and `take_redirects()` is never shipped down a socket") is closed.** Nothing in the crypto changed; this is wiring, and every check is still the existing one. **(1) WHERE.** Wired into the node's *own* listener (`server.rs` + `connection.rs`), **not** `backend/src/ws/game.rs` — that is the legacy central game WS from the pre-decentralization model and `backend` does not even depend on `magnetite-runtime`, so it was left untouched. Opt-in via `GameServerConfig::fleet: Option<FleetSession>`; `None` is byte-for-byte the old behaviour, which is what `magnetite node` and `magnetite dev` still pass. **(2) TRACKING.** The accept path calls `track_player(shard, player)` on connect and `untrack_player` on disconnect (and after a completed follow), so `shard_players` reflects live sessions rather than whatever a caller remembered to declare. A disconnected player is no longer minted a live credential by the next migration. **(3) DELIVERY.** A redirect pump drains `take_redirects()` every 20ms and sends `ServerNet::Redirect{SignedRedirect}` to that player's live socket; the connection loop treats a redirect as **terminal** — deliver, `Close`, drop — because the shard it was authoritative for now lives elsewhere. The queue is still filled from exactly one place (the success arm of `migrate_shard`, past a verified `CommitAck`), so the pump structurally cannot deliver a redirect for a rolled-back migration. **(4) ADMISSION.** `ClientNet::Follow{redirect}` goes straight to `FollowAdmission::admit` against `authority.epoch_of(shard)` — all eight refusals reused verbatim, none reimplemented — and only on success is the connection re-registered under the redirect's **original player id** (`ConnectionManager::register_as`, which refuses to displace a live session) and placed on the credentialed shard (`ShardManager::place`). That is what makes the session *continuous* instead of a fresh join. A refused follow **closes** the connection rather than degrading to an anonymous session. **(5) NODE-IDENTITY PROOF (new, additive).** Client-side redirect verification is only meaningful if the client knows which node key it is talking to, so `ClientNet::Hello{nonce}` → `ServerNet::NodeIdentity{node_key, nonce, sig}` lets a node prove possession of its key over a client-chosen nonce, under its own domain separator (`magnetite-node-hello-v1`) so the proof cannot be replayed as a redirect, follow token or discovery ad. **(6) JS CLIENT — it verifies.** `magnetite-web-client/src/follow.js` mirrors `SignedRedirect::verify_for` byte for byte: issuer must equal the pinned node key (checked **first**, so an injected redirect is inert), Ed25519 signature must verify, expiry and skew enforced, addressed to us, envelope/token agreement on all five bound fields — then on the new connection it pins `target_key`, makes the far side sign a fresh nonce, and aborts on key mismatch, wrong nonce, bad signature, close or timeout. **Crypto is WebCrypto `crypto.subtle` Ed25519 — no hand-rolled curve arithmetic and NO new JS dependency** (`@noble/ed25519` was not added: nothing is installable offline here, and WebCrypto is a vetted implementation available in Node 20+/Chrome 137+/Firefox 130+/Safari 17+). Where Ed25519 is unavailable it throws `unsupported` and the follow is **refused** — "cannot check" is never "checks out". `redirectUrl` keeps a `wss://` session from silently downgrading. `connection.js` handles the `redirect` frame itself (following a redirect is a security decision, not application logic) and only when `enableSessionFollow({nodeKey, …})` has supplied a key to verify against. **TESTS: runtime 115 lib + 4 doc + 9 integration (was 109 + 4; +6 follow unit, +7 socket-level, +2 fixture), frontend vitest 556 (was 535; +21).** The socket-level file runs two real `GameServer`s and a real `FleetNode` handoff listener on ephemeral ports and proves: a player connected to A ends up **attached on B under their original player id** and ticking (inputs Ack'd) after a real two-phase migration; the listener tracked both players without anyone calling `track_player` by hand; A closes the redirected connection; and the negatives — forged redirect (client `WrongIssuer` **and** B refusing the non-member issuer), expired redirect refused by client **and** independently by B, a redirect retargeted at another player refused with the token never consumed, a non-member issuer refused, a replayed redirect refused (nonce is one-shot), and **a failed migration delivering no redirect at all while the source keeps authority and the session is untouched**. `tests/redirect_fixture.rs` + `examples/redirect_fixture.rs` make the JS tests genuinely cross-language: the redirect the browser client verifies was signed by the Rust runtime, and a Rust test fails first if the wire format ever moves without the fixture being regenerated. No regressions: seams 35/52, sdk 327 (225+91+11 doc), backend 603, cli 17, sandbox 32, anticheat 48, e2e 18 — all green. Clippy: 0 new warnings (the 2 in `server.rs`/`tick.rs` are pre-existing). ESLint clean. **No new Rust dependency, no libp2p, no external service, offline only.** **REMAINING / HONEST LIMITS (now stated in `docs/hosting-a-server.md`, not implied away):** a redirect is a **bearer credential** — whoever reads it before redemption can redeem it once inside its ~30s window; single-use + epoch-fenced + short-lived bounds the damage but does not remove it, so run players over `wss://`. The node-identity proof authenticates the **key, not the channel**, so a relay in the middle of plaintext `ws://` is not defeated by it. **NAT traversal remains out of scope and unimplemented** — no hole punching, no relay; the redirect's address must be directly reachable. The `magnetite node` CLI still passes `fleet: None`, so session-follow is opt-in for callers that build a cluster in code. `FollowAdmission` still holds redeemed nonces until `clear_redeemed()` (bounded by the 30s TTL, not swept automatically). `game-client-bevy` deliberately does **not** follow redirects — it logs and stays put rather than reconnecting unverified; note its `bin` target has a **pre-existing** `NetConfig is private` compile error on `main.rs`, present at `d0d2e74` and untouched here. Still open from earlier waves: no automatic rebalancing or failure-driven re-placement, one TCP connection per migration, and the derived-route handoff-address TODO.
- [Fleet-CLI] DONE — `magnetite-cli/src/main.rs` (cluster flags + persisted node key + 13 tests), `magnetite-runtime/src/node.rs` (`NodeConfig::fleet` passthrough), `magnetite-seams/src/identity.rs` (`RawKeypairAuth::seed()` + 1 test), `game-client-bevy/src/main.rs`, `docs/hosting-a-server.md` + `site/docs/` mirror, `docs/index.md`, `docs/security/index.md` — **`magnetite node` can now actually run as a cluster member; the CLI no longer hardcodes `fleet: None`.** (1) MEMBERSHIP: `--cluster-peer <HEX>` (repeatable), `MAGNETITE_CLUSTER_PEERS` (comma/space list), `--cluster-peers-file` / `MAGNETITE_CLUSTER_PEERS_FILE` (one 64-hex key per line, `#` comments) — sources merge and de-dupe. **Deny-by-default preserved end to end:** an empty result is not an open door, it means no `FleetNode` is bound at all, no transport is built, and `fleet: None` is passed — byte-for-byte today's single-box node. When peers *are* configured, the SAME explicit key set is handed to both doors (`FleetNode::bind(allowed)` inbound, `NetworkHandoffTransport::with_membership` outbound); there is no code path passing `None`/empty as "allow anyone". A malformed key is a hard error naming the entry (and, for a file, its line number) rather than a dropped entry, and an unreadable peers file is an error, not an empty allowlist. (2) HANDOFF LISTENER: `--handoff-addr` / `MAGNETITE_HANDOFF_ADDR`, separate from the player-facing game port, defaulting to `<host>:<port+1>`; refuses to equal the game bind. Dropped when the serve loop exits, so the node-to-node door closes with the process. (3) NODE IDENTITY NOW PERSISTED (closes `TODO(node-key)`): first run generates an Ed25519 keypair from the OS CSPRNG and writes the seed `0600` to `--node-key-file` / `MAGNETITE_NODE_KEY_FILE` / `$MAGNETITE_HOME/node.key` / `~/.magnetite/node.key`; later runs reuse it, so identity survives restarts **and bind-address changes** — the tracker slot and every membership list that pinned the key stay valid. Pubkey + key source printed at startup for pasting into peers. `MAGNETITE_NODE_SEED` still overrides, but a malformed one now **refuses to boot** instead of silently booting under a different identity (that silent swap was the old failure mode). A loose-permission key file warns. Only when no key path can be determined at all does the old bind-address derivation remain, and the banner says `NOT STABLE`. (4) VERIFIED LIVE, not just unit-tested: two real `magnetite node` processes, each with the other's printed key, both bind their handoff listeners (`lsof`-confirmed) and report `Session follow : ON`; a run with no peers reports "hands shards to nobody" and binds nothing; `--cluster-peer deadbeef` exits non-zero with a length-explaining error; the key file is `0600` and the second run reports `(stable)`. (5) BEVY BIN FIXED (Task D, one line): `main.rs` imported `NetConfig` through `app`, where it is a private `use`; it now takes it from `net`, its defining module. `cargo build --bins` is green. (6) DOCS: `hosting-a-server.md` gains a copy-pasteable two-node walkthrough (print keys → cross-authorize → start both → capacity-driven placement → a player following a migration), a flag/env table, and a "node identity is a key file, not an address" section; the stale "the CLI does not enable it" bullet is replaced by the deny-by-default explanation. The honest limits are restated, not softened: **no NAT traversal, no hole punching, no relay — nodes must be directly reachable (same LAN / VPN / public IP with the port open), and WAN operation is untested**; a redirect is a bearer credential inside its ~30s window so run players over `wss://`; the node-identity proof authenticates the key, not the channel. `docs/index.md` and `docs/security/index.md` no longer claim the node keypair is an unimplemented stopgap. **TESTS: cli 30 (was 17; +13 covering deny-by-default, fail-loud parsing, file/env merge, allowlist pinning, key persistence and refusal of a malformed key file), seams 36 lib / 53 with `--features keyname` (was 35/52; +1 seed round-trip). No regressions: runtime 115 lib + 4 doc + 9 integration, sdk 327 `--features scaling`, backend 603, sandbox 32, anticheat 48, e2e 18 — all green.** Clippy: 0 new warnings (cli's 1 and runtime's 2 are pre-existing). No new dependency, no libp2p, offline only. **REMAINING:** the CLI binds the cluster door and wires session-follow but does **not** yet drive migrations — no CLI-level autoscaler observing discovery ads through `RouteDirectory` and rebalancing shards, so placement across nodes still requires calling the scheduler/transport from code (documented as a TODO in `hosting-a-server.md`). Also unchanged from earlier waves: one TCP connection per migration, `FollowAdmission` nonces are TTL-bounded but not swept, and there is no key-rotation story — replacing `node.key` means re-pasting the new pubkey into every peer.

- [Fleet-Rebalance] DONE — `magnetite-runtime/src/rebalance.rs` (new, ~800 lines incl. 14 unit tests), `magnetite-runtime/tests/cluster_rebalance.rs` (new, 10 multi-node socket tests), `magnetite-runtime/src/fleet.rs` (read-only `StatusRequest`/`Status` frames + `probe_peer` + `CapacityPublisher`), `magnetite-runtime/src/cluster.rs` (`RouteDirectory::admit_operator_route`), `magnetite-runtime/src/lib.rs`, `magnetite-cli/src/main.rs` (`<hex>@<addr>` peers, rebalance flags, background loop, +7 tests), `docs/hosting-a-server.md` + `site/docs/` mirror — **Closes the gap every prior fleet wave left open: nothing drove migrations, so three configured nodes would sit there with every shard on whichever one created it.** Nothing below weakens the existing guarantees: deny-by-default membership, key pinning, the epoch fence, two-phase commit and every `FollowAdmission` check are untouched, and a rebalancer decision is only ever a *proposal* — the move itself still goes through `migrate_shard`, which still fails closed with the source owning the shard. **(1) THE RECONCILER.** `Rebalancer::tick` reads live routes from `RouteDirectory` (signature-verified, lease-checked, membership-filtered), probes each member for what it holds and how big it is, runs `SpreadScheduler` over the visible cluster, and sheds whatever it is holding beyond its own capacity share. **(2) SEEING THE CLUSTER.** The `Discovery` seam returns unsigned `SessionAd`s with no node key, so a node had no honest way to learn peer load. Added two **read-only** frames to the already-authenticated handoff wire: `StatusRequest`/`Status`, answered only past `server_handshake` (which has already enforced the inbound allowlist), mutating nothing and touching no authority. The reply is deliberately unsigned — it travels inside the authenticated channel, so its authorship is exactly as proven as every other post-handshake frame — and it is **advisory**: a member that lies about its capacity can only attract or repel shards it was already authorized to hold, and every actual handoff to it is still membership-checked, key-pinned, two-phase and epoch-fenced. Documented as such rather than implied to be a trust boundary. **(3) FOUR BRAKES, ON BY DEFAULT.** A reconciler that reacts to every measurement is worse than none. `deadband_shards: 1` (a greedy bin-pack routinely differs by one shard for pure tie-breaking reasons; reacting to that is how thrash starts), `cooldown: 120s` per shard (comfortably longer than one 30s pass, so a shard cannot be re-judged by the next, staler, view), `max_in_flight: 2` per pass (enough to drain a lopsided node in a few passes, few enough that reconnect storms stay small), and per-peer exponential backoff `5s → ×2 → 300s` where a **backed-off peer is not even probed** — that is the difference between backing off and merely retrying more slowly. **(4) WHY IT CONVERGES, AND HOW THAT IS PROVEN.** Two design choices carry it. The desired placement is a **pure function of the shard set and the node set** — it never reads current ownership — so moving a shard cannot change where anything is supposed to be; each successful move strictly reduces `Σ|actual−desired|`, a non-negative integer, so the process must terminate. And we **balance counts, not identities**: a node asked to swap three shards for three different ones does nothing, since identity-based diffing is the classic source of endless shuffling. The scheduler is consulted for *how many* shards each node should hold; targets are then chosen by **deficit**, most-starved first, tie-broken on key hex so every node computes the same order from the same facts. Asserted directly, not argued: `steady_state_issues_no_migrations` (unit) drives a cluster to a fixed point and then requires ten further passes to be empty, and `convergence_then_zero_migrations` (socket, 3 real nodes, 9 shards) requires **twenty** further passes to migrate exactly nothing and asserts ownership did not drift. **(5) FAILURE-DRIVEN RE-PLACEMENT, TOLD TRUTHFULLY.** **There is no state replication. A node that dies takes its shards' in-memory state with it and that state is gone.** The rebalancer detects it (a peer that stops answering or drops out of the live route set, holding shards no surviving node now reports), reports each as a distinct `ShardLoss` whose `Display` says `STATE LOST` and `no state replication`, logs it at warn, prints it once per loss (not once per tick — an operator would otherwise think it kept happening), and **does not start replacement shards**. That refusal is the point: an empty shard with the same id would look like a successful recovery in every log line and metric while every player in it silently lost their session. Surviving nodes do stop routing new work to the dead peer immediately, which is re-placement of *capacity*, not recovery of *state*, and the docs say exactly that. TODO(state-replication) is recorded in the module docs and the hosting guide as the honest long-term fix (warm standby or blob-store checkpointing), deliberately not attempted here — it needs quorum rules, a split-brain story against the epoch fence, and a checkpoint cadence. **(6) CLI.** `--cluster-peer` now accepts `<hex>@<host:port>`. The key is still the authorization and the address is only a location: `admit_operator_route` refuses an address for a non-member exactly as `observe` does, and the handshake still aborts unless the far side proves control of the pinned key, so a stolen address gets nothing. A bare key remains a full member (it may hand us shards, its follows are admitted) with nowhere to send work. `key@` with an empty address is a hard error — almost always a truncated config line, and treating it as "member with no address" would quietly remove that node from every placement decision. **The loop is ON by default whenever at least one peer is routable**, justified in the docs: a cluster told who its members are and how to reach them, which then refuses to distribute work, is the bug this wave exists to fix, so leaving it opt-in would ship the broken default. It is off when nothing is routable (exactly the deny-by-default case) and `--no-rebalance` turns it off explicitly. `--rebalance-interval/-deadband/-max-in-flight` expose the brakes. Peer-visible capacity is the same measured number already advertised to the phonebook — one source, published via `CapacityPublisher`; a node that has not published claims **zero** headroom, so an unmeasured box attracts nothing rather than a share it cannot hold. **TESTS: runtime 129 lib + 4 doc + 19 integration (was 115 + 4 + 9; +14 unit, +10 socket), cli 37 (was 30; +7).** The socket file stands up real `FleetNode`s on ephemeral ports and proves: 10 shards distribute across 6/3/1-capacity nodes with share tracking capacity and the 1-shard node never overfilled; a joining node takes share; convergence then twenty silent passes; a shard in cooldown is not re-moved even when handed back; an unreachable peer is probed **once** and then not contacted again inside the backoff window (failure count stays at 1 across five passes); a failed migration leaves the source owning all four shards with byte-identical state; a dead peer's shards are reported as loss with the right cause and owner, mourned once, and **not** silently taken over; a lapsed peer receives nothing and resumes when its route returns; and a genuinely-running non-member is refused entry to the route directory and receives nothing. No regressions: seams 36 / 53 (`--features keyname`), sdk 327 (`--features scaling`), sandbox 32, anticheat 48, e2e green, backend 603 and frontend 556 untouched by construction (no backend/sdk/frontend file changed). Clippy: **0 new warnings** (runtime's 2 in `server.rs`/`tick.rs` and cli's 1 in `validate_crate_name` are pre-existing). **No new dependency, no libp2p, no external service, offline only.** **REMAINING / HONEST LIMITS:** NAT traversal stays out of scope and unimplemented — a rebalancer cannot route around an unroutable node, it can only back off and place work elsewhere. Peer addresses are operator-configured because the `Discovery` seam's `find` returns unsigned ads with no node key; deriving handoff routes from *signed* ads still needs a handoff-address field on `SessionAd`, which changes `signing_bytes` and so wants a deliberate seam-version bump. Placement is per-node and independent: each node plans over the cluster it can see and only moves shards it owns, which is what makes it safe without consensus, but it means a partitioned pair can briefly hold different views (bounded by the deadband and cooldown, not eliminated). Peer capacity is self-reported and placement is not a defence against a dishonest *member*. Unchanged from earlier waves: one TCP connection per migration, `FollowAdmission` nonces are TTL-bounded but not swept, and there is no key-rotation story.

- [W1-INPUT] done — `magnetite-seams/src/input.rs` (new), `magnetite-seams/src/{lib.rs,error.rs}`, `DECENTRALIZATION.md` §3.7 — **`InputProvider` seam (§3.7) added, drawing the deterministic/attested guarantee boundary explicitly.** Motivated by `wibbly/WIBBLY.md` §6: wibbly is a camera-gesture client that will consume magnetite as its platform, and gesture input is the one input class `verify_replay` cannot cover. New `InputClass::{Deterministic,Attested}` is the load-bearing type — `is_replay_verifiable()` lets the "may I treat this as evidence?" decision be made in code rather than from memory. `InputEvent` is an enum (not a struct with a flag) so a consumer must match on the class before reading the payload. `trait InputProvider { class / submit / drain / plausibility_limits }`; both shipped providers **fail closed on class mismatch** — `LocalDeviceInput` (the default: deterministic keyboard/gamepad queue, zero deps, replay-verifiable) refuses attested events, and `AttestedEventInput` refuses deterministic commands rather than silently *downgrading* input that had the replay guarantee. `PlausibilityGate` screens attested events per player: rate limit, per-kind cooldown, human-reachable velocity (default 20 m/s), confidence floor, timestamp skew/staleness, monotonic sequence (replay). Screening state advances **only on acceptance**, so rejected floods cannot evict an honest player's rate budget. `SignedAttestedEvent` binds an event to the claiming key (stops forging in another player's name, stops relay edits) — documented throughout as proving **authorship, not truth**. `SeamError::Implausible` added. `DefaultSeams` gains a deterministic `input` slot so the default bundle stays fully replay-verifiable and depends on no camera. **Honesty:** nothing here *produces* a gesture event — no camera capture, no pose model, no vendor code, wibbly is not a dependency, and no camera client is wired up in this repo. The seam is the socket, and today only the socket. A test (`a_plausible_synthetic_event_is_indistinguishable_from_a_real_one`) asserts that a hand-fabricated, correctly-signed, in-human-range event passes every check there is — the ceiling of this input class, pinned in code so it cannot be quietly forgotten. Tests: seams 73 lib (was 56) + 4 integration, `cargo check`/`cargo test`/`cargo clippy --all-features --all-targets` clean. Legacy `GAPS.md`/`TASKS.md`/`DECISIONS.md` deliberately NOT updated — they predate the redesign (DECISIONS.md still records the reversed fiat-only pivot); this log is the live record.

# Magnetite — Autonomous Build Decisions & Design System

> **[2026-07-20] PARTLY SUPERSEDED — historical record.**
> Moved here from the repository root. This document is kept for the record, not
> as current guidance. In particular the **"PAYMENTS PIVOT — remove crypto → Wise
> for payouts" decision immediately below was later REVERSED**: Magnetite is now
> non-custodial, there is no fiat on-ramp, and Paystack/Wise/custodial balances/
> the 70/30 split were deleted from the codebase. For the current design see
> [`DECENTRALIZATION.md`](../../DECENTRALIZATION.md) and
> [Payments](../payments.md). Decisions unrelated to payments may still hold —
> check them against the code before relying on them.

---

## ⚑ PAYMENTS PIVOT (2026-06-01, user directive): REMOVE CRYPTO → WISE FOR PAYOUTS
**Crypto/USDC/Circle is removed entirely. The platform is fiat-only.** Grounded decisions (Wave PAY):
- **D-PAY-1 — Currency:** Wallet/earnings/marketplace are denominated in **USD** (fiat). Remove all "USDC",
  Circle, on-chain wallet-address, and ZAR→USDC concepts. `currency.js` default → `USD`; drop `formatUSDC`.
- **D-PAY-2 — Payouts → Wise:** Developer payouts go through the **Wise (TransferWise) API**. New
  `services/wise.rs` client: create/store a Wise **recipient** per developer (bank/email), then quote →
  transfer → fund. Env: `WISE_API_TOKEN`, `WISE_PROFILE_ID`, `WISE_SANDBOX` (uses api.sandbox.transferwise.tech).
  Unconfigured → explicit error (HTTP 502 "payouts not configured"), NEVER fake success; `WISE_SANDBOX=true`
  returns clearly-labelled sandbox results for dev. `payout.rs::process_single_payout` calls Wise (not Circle).
- **D-PAY-3 — Deposits/top-ups & subscriptions:** keep **Paystack** (fiat on-ramp) for adding funds + paid
  subscriptions; remove the Circle deposit path and the Circle deposit-webhook gap. Card/bank top-ups stay fiat.
- **D-PAY-4 — Withdraw = payout:** wallet/developer "withdraw" creates a payout request row that the existing
  spawned payout job processes via Wise. No on-chain transfer.
- **D-PAY-5 — SDK:** `platform::marketplace::PaymentMethod::Usd` stays (now means fiat USD); fix the doc that
  says "USDC (Circle)". Keep `Paystack` + `Points` variants. Remove `Circle`/crypto references in docs/copy.
- **D-PAY-6 — Marketing copy:** drop "crypto"/"USDC"/"real money no middlemen → crypto" framing; reframe as
  fiat payouts via Wise, Paystack on-ramp. The 70/30 split is unchanged.
- Bucket D after this: live **WISE_API_TOKEN** + Paystack keys (code real, honest error without them);
  the former "Circle deposit webhook" Bucket-D item is removed.

> Single source of truth for the autonomous multi-wave rebuild. Every agent reads this
> file before working. The orchestrator audits against it every 30 minutes.

Last updated: 2026-06-03 (INFRA-E2E Agent 1 — magnetite-runtime deployability)

**Goal:** Prove the local stack runs end-to-end via real WebSocket clients; add perf bench report; add `scripts/e2e-play.sh`. Agent 2 owns `magnetite-e2e/` + `scripts/e2e-play.sh` ONLY.

**Deliverables shipped:**
- `magnetite-e2e/tests/fullstack_ws.rs` (NEW, 476 lines) — 3 full-stack tests:
  1. `fullstack_ws_welcome_snapshot_delta_ack_and_replay_clean` — binds an ephemeral TCP port, starts a real `GameServer` (NativeExecutor/ArenaShooter), connects 3 independent `tokio-tungstenite` WS clients speaking `ClientNet`/`ServerNet`, drives 10 rounds of inputs, asserts: all clients receive `Welcome` + `Snapshot` + `Delta`; input pipeline live (Ack or Reject for all 30 inputs); two independent `NativeExecutor` runs converge (same `state_hash` every tick); `verify_replay` → `Clean`.
  2. `fullstack_ws_snapshot_ticks_are_monotonic` — asserts the authoritative tick counter never decreases.
  3. `fullstack_ws_dedicated_topology_smoke` — verifies the `Dedicated{tick_hz:30, max_players:32}` topology path starts and broadcasts state correctly.

**Crossroads:**

| # | Decision | Choice | Rationale |
|---|----------|--------|-----------|
| E2E-2-1 | Ack vs Ack-or-Reject assertion | Accept Ack OR Reject as "input processed" | `ArenaShooter::validate` returns `Unauthorized` for players not `on_join`'d (by design — WS path doesn't call it; on_join is a runtime-host concern). The input pipeline IS working: inputs reach the executor, get validated, and a `Reject` frame is sent back. Asserting Ack-only would couple the test to the game's internal join state rather than the protocol pipeline. |
| E2E-2-2 | snapshot_every for WS test | 3 | `snapshot_every:1` sends only Snapshots (no Deltas — the delta branch never runs); `snapshot_every:3` gives bootstrap Snapshot on tick 1, Delta on tick 2, Snapshot on tick 3, proving BOTH frame types flow through the server. |
| E2E-2-3 | Wasm in fullstack test | Not included | WasmExecutor requires a pre-built artifact. The wasm pipeline is fully proven in `wasm_end_to_end.rs`. The fullstack test is the network/game-loop proof and must run on `cargo test` with no prerequisites. |
| E2E-2-4 | WS round-trip bench "no samples" | Pre-existing issue, not fixed | The existing `ws_round_trip_latency_bench` waits for `Ack{seq}` but ArenaShooter returns Reject (unjoined player). This is a pre-existing design in the bench code (owned by a prior wave). The bench exits 0. The in-proc `scale_bench` numbers are the canonical perf report. |

Verification: `docker compose config --services` lists `mediamtx`; merged config
shows all four ports, health check, volume mount, and `MEDIA_SERVER_BASE_URL`
wired to backend. Grep confirms 9 mediamtx references across both compose files.

## 1. Product Vision (refined)

**Magnetite is the open-source platform for building, distributing, and monetizing
Rust games — that scale from a weekend game jam to a COD-size AAA title.**

- **Rust-first.** Game logic is authored in Rust. Clients compile Bevy → WASM (browser)
  and to native. Servers are server-authoritative Rust, sandboxed.
- **Scales with the game.** A tiny single-file arcade game and a large multiplayer title
  use the same SDK and platform; the platform provides the heavy lifting (hosting,
  matchmaking, real-time netcode, persistence, payments) so developers only write game logic.
- **Distribution built in.** A storefront/marketplace distributes games; players discover,
  play (in-browser via WASM or native), and pay.
- **Open source.** Platform (MIT), SDK (MIT), game template (MIT), docs (CC0).
- **Real money, no middlemen.** USDC payments (Circle), Paystack fiat on-ramp, playtime-based
  developer payouts, 30% platform fee (70/30 split — implemented in marketplace + payout).

The previous "HTML5 games" framing is **deprecated** — all copy/marketing pivots to the
Rust-games-at-any-scale narrative above.

### 1b. Gaming Suite (expanded scope — 2026-05-30 user directive)

Magnetite is not just a host/store — it is a **unified gaming suite** where every game, simple or AAA,
is built on one SDK and plugs into shared platform services. New pillars:

- **Communities & comms (Discord-class):** servers/guilds → channels (text + voice), DMs, presence,
  roles/permissions, real-time chat, **voice ("speaking")**, and **streaming** (go live + watch).
  The SAME comms system powers **in-game chat and voice** (a lobby/match auto-provisions a voice+text room
  and an in-game overlay). Players can also **stream out** to external services (Twitch/YouTube via RTMP).
- **Build any game on one system:** from a tiny 2D arcade jam game to an **advanced FPS** or a
  **motorsport game with complex 3D graphics & physics** — all via the same `magnetite-sdk` + Bevy/rapier,
  with graphics/engine tiers so simple games stay lightweight and advanced games scale up.
- **Controllers:** first-class **game-controller / gamepad** input through the SDK (Gamepad API on web,
  gilrs natively), with a unified input-mapping layer.
- **Points & score economy:** a platform-wide **points/XP/score system** games submit to and spend from
  (rewards, ranks, seasonal resets), built on the existing leaderboard/scores foundation.
- **Dev-run paid marketplaces:** developers can run **in-game stores** (cosmetics, items, DLC, passes) and
  use a shared catalog/checkout with revenue share, built on the existing USDC/Paystack payment rails.
- **Central services games can call:** identity/wallet, comms (chat/voice), points, leaderboards,
  achievements, matchmaking, cloud saves, the marketplace, and anti-cheat — one SDK surface.
